claims.text: The WHEN method tells the coffee pot that sufficient milk has been introduced into the coffee.
claims.reason: The WHEN method claim is supported by the sufficient-milk sentence and the explicit WHEN method sentence.

claims.text: The Content-Type header of a POST or BREW request sent to a TEA-capable pot MUST be "message/teapot" if tea is to be requested.
claims.reason: The required Content-Type is quoted with its POST/BREW and tea condition.

claims.text: A TEA-capable pot that receives a BREW message of content type "message/teapot" MUST respond in accordance with the URI requested.
claims.reason: The extra URI-response statement repeats its cited requirement without broadening scope.

claims.text: HTCPCP-TEA updates the Accept-Additions header field to allow addition-type options including sugar-type.
claims.reason: The updated addition-type grammar includes sugar-type; the source section identifies the Accept-Additions field.

claims.text: The permitted sugar-type additions are "Sugar", "Xylitol", and "Stevia".
claims.reason: All three sugar alternatives match the quoted grammar; no fourth alternative is invented.

claims.text: Coffee pots SHOULD use the Network Time Protocol [NTP] to synchronize their clocks to a globally accurate time standard.
claims.reason: SHOULD, NTP and synchronization to globally accurate time are all retained.

claims.text: The 428 status code indicates that the origin server requires the request to be conditional.
claims.reason: 428 requires the request to be conditional.

claims.text: Its typical use is to avoid the "lost update" problem.
claims.reason: Typical lost-update prevention matches the quote; it is not made an unconditional guarantee.

claims.text: The 428 status code is optional; clients cannot rely upon its use to prevent "lost update" conflicts.
claims.reason: The optional-code caveat and inability to rely upon it match the security-section quote.

claims.text: HTTP 429 responses MAY include a Retry-After header indicating how long to wait before making a new request.
claims.reason: MAY and waiting-time meaning match; it is not changed to MUST.

claims.text: The 429 status code indicates that the user has sent too many requests in a given amount of time ("rate limiting").
claims.reason: The rate-limiting description is quoted exactly.

claims.text: Responses with the 429 status code MUST NOT be stored by a cache.
claims.reason: The extra cache prohibition preserves MUST NOT and code 429.

claims.text: Responses with the 431 status code MUST NOT be stored by a cache.
claims.reason: The complete 431 prohibition is quoted and the MUST NOT negation is unchanged.

claims.text: TEA-capable pots that are not provisioned to brew coffee may return either a status code of 503 or a code of 418.
claims.reason: The not-provisioned-to-brew-coffee condition and optional 503/418 alternatives are retained.
503 is correctly described as temporary coffee unavailability.

claims.text: 418 is defined in the base HTCPCP specification to denote a more permanent indication that the pot is a teapot.
claims.reason: 418 is correctly described as the more permanent teapot indication; the answer never claims it is mandatory.
